title: Jill Biden Feared Joe Was Having a Stroke During 2024 Debate
text:
Jill Biden's new book, View from the East Wing: A Memoir, reveals her fears for her husband's health during the 2024 debate. A Democratic Party autopsy has also criticized the White House for prioritizing Jill over Kamala Harris.
Jill Biden feared her husband was having a stroke on live television during the disastrous debate with Donald Trump that ultimately sank his reelection campaign.
She said she was frightened, as she had never seen Joe like that before or since. Biden appeared frail and stumbled over his words during his infamous June 2024 clash with Trump, marking a watershed moment when Democratic allies began publicly questioning his fitness for office. Jill Biden was one of Biden's closest confidantes and a driving force behind his 2024 reelection bid.
She fiercely advocated for him to stay in the race after the debate and had a tense relationship with his ultimate successor for the Democratic candidacy, Kamala Harris. Biden was forced to drop out just weeks later, and since leaving office, he has been diagnosed with an aggressive form of prostate cancer that has spread to his bones.
Jill Biden's stunning admission to CBS News comes just days before the release of her new book, View from the East Wing: A Memoir. The book's release coincides with a bombshell Democratic Party autopsy that underlined how Jill was prioritized over Harris by the White House during the 2024 election. The report states Biden's White House lavished polling and strategy on Jill, while leaving Harris so neglected that aides had no research prepared when she was thrust onto the ticket.
The 192-page dossier commissioned by the Democratic National Committee (DNC) wrote that the Biden White House ordered extensive polling on the settings, issues, and messaging Dr Jill should use to support her husband's presidency. However, no equivalent research was ever commissioned for Harris, leaving pollsters scrambling to get three emergency studies into the field the moment Biden stepped aside in July 2024. Kamala Harris and Jill Biden had a tense relationship in the White House, according to the report.
The author, veteran Democratic strategist Paul Rivera, brands the failure a 'massive missed opportunity' and concludes the White House never positioned or prepared its own Vice President to face Trump. The dossier was initially published by CNN with heavy annotations from the DNC disputing the accuracy of many of the report's claims
